item.title: Winners!
item.content:encoded:
First, thank you all for all the amazing entries in both categories. This contest has been a blast to read, and I hope future writers take note and inspiration here to continue to create amazing things. Thank you to Dexanote for running this as well; he should be taking the vast majority of the credit here.

The winners are:

SCP-2439 by Jack Ike, SCP-2669 by Kalinin and History by Humanmale. Congrats! Your works will be featured on the main page for the entirety of October; plus, you'll get the satisfaction of having won a contest!

The runner-ups in both categories are as follows:

SCPs:

  • SCP-2959 by kinchtheknifeblade
  • SCP-2193 by Shaggydredlocks

Tales:

  • Cat In A Box by LurkD
  • And What Was a Soul to That Blank White World by Cyantreuse, After The End by weizhong, and D-5111 by Jacob Conwell

Thank you to everyone for participating! Dexanote may be making a post soon. The hub page has been updated as well. This was a fun contest <3

item.title: It Begins - The Contest is Open.
item.content:encoded:
I'm opening this just a few minutes early, because in the grand scheme of things, it doesn't matter terribly.

Entries posted after the posted end-time of 23:59 PM EST on Monday September 26th will not be accepted into the contest.

Vote standings as of approximately 23:39 PM EST on Friday, September 30th will be counted for the contest winners. The announcement will be made sometime in the early morning of October 1, 2016.

Have at it.

EDIT: I will eventually post personal reflections or reviews of each individual SCP and Tale entry when the Contest is over. I will post them early, if I feel certain entries are 'on a threshold' and toe the line between fulfilling requirements and not (which will probably be most -Js). Any ones I feel the need to disqualify will get a review after I have spoken directly to the author, via IRC or PMs.

item.content:encoded:
Correct, only the votes/text of a single part is considered, no matter the length. Remember, this contest is done by total votes in response to the content of the piece, and how well they fulfill contest requirements - shedding light on D-Class personnel.

Chances are, the front page of the SCP will be the most heavily upvoted part anyway. See: 093, 087, and my own 097, wherein the logs are important and highly upvoted but also pale in comparison to the main page's upvotes. You COULD have it all on one page, but I doubt that'd actually make a huge difference. People will upvote the main SCP if it's good, and they'll upvote the main SCP if the logs are great.

That particular rule was written with Tale series in mind, so we're clear, but applies to SCP entries too.
